scope: Genesis 12–25; all 394 verses. Earlier Genesis 1–11 and James revisions remain unchanged.

source.verse_hash_method: SHA-256 of the exact UTF-8 <verse ...>...</verse> substring, including markup, whitespace, written forms, and any reading notes. No XML reserialization or Hebrew normalization.

delta_method: F0 retained wording; F1 lexical; F2 syntax/idiom; F3 consequential interpretive or textual choice. These are editorial assessments, separate from similarity scores. Independent editorial review has not occurred.

verses.rationale: Unfold the three departures and destination without assigning an unstated location.
verses.before: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your land, your kindred, and your father’s house to the land that I will show you.
verses.after: The LORD said to Abram, “Leave your land, your relatives, and your father's household. Go to the land I will show you.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the LORD said to Abram, “Go from your land, your kindred, and your father’s house to the land that I will show you.

verses.rationale: Keep nation, blessing, and name as distinct promises; render the final imperative as a direct commission.
verses.before: I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.
verses.after: I will make you a great nation and bless you. I will make your name great. Be a blessing.
verses.tsw_comparator: And I will make of you a great nation, and I will bless you, and make your name great, so that you will be a blessing.

verses.rationale: Distinguish contempt from curse; preserve worldwide family scope and passive blessing with reflexive alternative noted.
verses.before: I will bless people who bless you, and the one who treats you lightly I will treat lightly; and in you all the families of the earth will be blessed.”
verses.after: I will bless those who bless you, and curse whoever treats you with contempt. Through you all the families of the earth will be blessed.”
verses.tsw_comparator: I will bless those who bless you, and the one who treats you lightly I will treat lightly; and in you all the families of the earth shall be blessed.”

verses.rationale: Keep obedience, Lot, departure place, and age in two readable sentences.
verses.before: So Abram went, as the LORD had spoken to him; and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.
verses.after: Abram went as the LORD had told him, and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five when he left Haran.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Abram went, as the LORD had spoken to him; and Lot went with him. Abram was seventy-five years old when he departed from Haran.

verses.rationale: Clarify kinship and journey; retain acquisition of people rather than assume converts or free employees.
verses.before: Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions that they had gathered, and the persons that they had acquired in Haran; and they set out to go to the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,
verses.after: He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all the possessions they had gathered, and the people they had acquired in Haran. They set out for Canaan and arrived there.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abram took Sarai his wife, and Lot his brother’s son, and all the possessions that they had gathered, and the persons that they had acquired in Haran; and they set out to go to the land of Canaan. When they came to the land of Canaan,

verses.rationale: Preserve named tree and existing inhabitants; note oak/terebinth uncertainty.
verses.before: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.
verses.after: Abram traveled through the land as far as Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. The Canaanites were living in the land at that time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abram passed through the land to the place of Shechem, to the oak of Moreh. At that time the Canaanites were in the land.

verses.rationale: Retain appearance, land, descendants, and repeated divine encounter.
verses.before: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built there an altar to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.after: The LORD appeared to Abram and said, “I will give this land to your descendants.” Abram built an altar there to the LORD, who had appeared to him.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, “To your offspring I will give this land.” So he built there an altar to the LORD, who had appeared to him.

verses.rationale: Make compass directions clear and preserve altar and invocation.
verses.before: From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and there he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.
verses.after: From there he moved into the hills east of Bethel and pitched his tent, with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east. There he built an altar to the LORD and called on the LORD's name.
verses.tsw_comparator: From there he moved on to the hill country east of Bethel, and pitched his tent, with Bethel on the west and Ai on the east; and there he built an altar to the LORD and called on the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Render repeated journeying naturally while retaining the southern region.
verses.before: Abram journeyed on by stages toward the Negeb.
verses.after: Abram moved on, traveling in stages toward the Negev.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Abram journeyed on by stages toward the Negeb.

verses.rationale: Keep famine as the reason and temporary residence as the purpose.
verses.before: Now there was a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.
verses.after: A famine struck the land. Because it was severe, Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a time.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now there was a famine in the land, so Abram went down to Egypt to sojourn there, for the famine was severe in the land.

verses.rationale: Keep beauty because the speaker explicitly names it.
verses.before: When he was about to enter Egypt, he said to Sarai his wife, “Look now, I know that you are a woman beautiful in appearance;
verses.after: As he approached Egypt, he said to his wife Sarai, “I know you are a beautiful woman.

verses.rationale: Preserve the contrast as Abram's prediction rather than the narrator's judgment.

verses.rationale: Retain both personal benefit and survival; do not soften Abram's self-interest.

verses.after: Please say you are my sister, so that things will go well for me because of you, and my life will be spared on your account.”

verses.rationale: Retain this clear sentence or speech introduction after source review; no change is needed for distinctiveness alone.

verses.after: When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.
verses.tsw_comparator: When Abram entered Egypt, the Egyptians saw that the woman was very beautiful.

verses.rationale: Keep passive taking without inventing Sarai's consent.
verses.before: And when the officials of Pharaoh saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.
verses.after: Pharaoh's officials saw her and praised her to Pharaoh, and she was taken into Pharaoh's household.
verses.tsw_comparator: And when the officials of Pharaoh saw her, they praised her to Pharaoh, and the woman was taken into Pharaoh’s house.

verses.rationale: Preserve property categories and enslaved people's status in a readable inventory.
verses.before: And for her sake he treated Abram well; and he had sheep, oxen, male donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.
verses.after: Pharaoh treated Abram well because of her. Abram received sheep and goats, cattle, male and female donkeys, male and female slaves, and camels.
verses.tsw_comparator: And for her sake he treated Abram well; and he had sheep, oxen, male donkeys, male and female servants, female donkeys, and camels.

verses.rationale: Keep divine agency and the explicit marriage identification.
verses.before: But the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.
verses.after: But the LORD struck Pharaoh and his household with severe afflictions because of Sarai, Abram's wife.
verses.tsw_comparator: But the LORD afflicted Pharaoh and his house with great plagues because of Sarai, Abram’s wife.

verses.rationale: Separate summons from the two accusations.
verses.before: Then Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?
verses.after: Pharaoh summoned Abram. “What have you done to me?” he asked. “Why did you not tell me she was your wife?
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Pharaoh called Abram and said, “What is this that you have done to me? Why did you not tell me that she was your wife?

verses.rationale: Retain Pharaoh's marriage claim and abrupt dismissal.
verses.before: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife; take her, and go.”
verses.after: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her as my wife? Here is your wife. Take her and go!”
verses.tsw_comparator: Why did you say, ‘She is my sister,’ so that I took her to be my wife? Now then, here is your wife; take her, and go.”

verses.rationale: Clarify the subject of the orders and preserve the entire departing household's possessions.
verses.before: Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him; and they sent him away, along with his wife and all that he had.
verses.after: Pharaoh gave his men orders about Abram, and they sent him away with his wife and everything he had.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Pharaoh gave men orders concerning him; and they sent him away, along with his wife and all that he had.

verses.rationale: Keep the return direction and Lot as a distinct companion.
verses.before: So Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the Negev.
verses.after: Abram went up from Egypt to the Negev with his wife and everything he had. Lot went with him.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Abram went up from Egypt, he and his wife and all that he had, and Lot with him, into the Negev.

verses.rationale: Render heavy as wealth while preserving its three forms.
verses.before: Now Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.
verses.after: Abram was very wealthy in livestock, silver, and gold.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Abram was very rich in livestock, in silver, and in gold.

verses.rationale: Preserve the return to the earlier campsite and continue into the altar reference.
verses.before: And he journeyed by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,
verses.after: He traveled in stages from the Negev to Bethel, back to the place between Bethel and Ai where he had first pitched his tent,
verses.tsw_comparator: And he journeyed by stages from the Negev as far as Bethel, to the place where his tent had been at the beginning, between Bethel and Ai,

verses.rationale: Keep altar, previous visit, and repeated invocation together.
verses.before: to the place of the altar that he had made there at first. And there Abram called upon the name of the LORD.
verses.after: where he had built the altar before. There Abram called on the LORD's name.
verses.tsw_comparator: to the place of the altar that he had made there at first. And there Abram called upon the name of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve all three possessions that prepare the conflict.
verses.before: Lot, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents,
verses.after: Lot, who traveled with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Lot, who went with Abram, also had flocks and herds and tents,

verses.rationale: Retain the repeated inability to remain together and its material cause.
verses.before: so that the land could not support both of them dwelling together, for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together.
verses.after: The land could not support them living together. Their possessions were so great that they could no longer stay together.
verses.tsw_comparator: so that the land could not support both of them dwelling together, for their possessions were so great that they could not dwell together.

verses.rationale: Make the conflicting groups explicit and retain the other inhabitants.
verses.before: And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were dwelling in the land.
verses.after: Quarrels broke out between Abram's herders and Lot's herders. The Canaanites and Perizzites were also living in the land then.
verses.tsw_comparator: And there was strife between the herdsmen of Abram’s livestock and the herdsmen of Lot’s livestock. At that time the Canaanites and the Perizzites were dwelling in the land.

verses.rationale: Render brothers as kinship appropriate to uncle and nephew.
verses.before: Then Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are kin.
verses.after: Abram said to Lot, “Please, let there be no quarrel between us or between our herders. We are family.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Abram said to Lot, “Let there be no strife between me and you, and between my herdsmen and your herdsmen, for we are kin.

verses.rationale: Retain reciprocal directions without replacing them with an inferred map.
verses.before: Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, then I will go to the right; or if you go to the right, then I will go to the left.”
verses.after: The whole land is before you. Please separate from me. If you go left, I will go right; if you go right, I will go left.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Is not the whole land before you? Separate yourself from me. If you go to the left, then I will go to the right; or if you go to the right, then I will go to the left.”

verses.rationale: Unfold the description and parenthetical timing without losing either comparison.
verses.before: Lot lifted up his eyes and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered everywhere—before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar.
verses.after: Lot looked out over the whole Jordan plain. It was well watered all the way to Zoar, like the LORD's garden, like the land of Egypt. This was before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Lot lifted up his eyes and saw that the whole plain of the Jordan was well watered everywhere—before the LORD destroyed Sodom and Gomorrah—like the garden of the LORD, like the land of Egypt, in the direction of Zoar.

verses.rationale: Choose the directional eastward reading and note the possible from-east construction.

verses.after: Lot chose the whole Jordan plain for himself and traveled east. So the two separated.
verses.tsw_comparator: So Lot chose for himself all the plain of the Jordan, and Lot journeyed eastward. Thus they separated from one another.

verses.rationale: Preserve the contrast and Lot's movement toward Sodom.
verses.before: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled among the cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.
verses.after: Abram settled in Canaan, while Lot settled among the towns of the plain and pitched his tents as far as Sodom.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abram settled in the land of Canaan, while Lot settled among the cities of the plain and moved his tent as far as Sodom.

verses.rationale: Keep both wrongdoing and its relation to the LORD without specifying an offense here.
verses.before: Now the people of Sodom were exceedingly wicked, sinners against the LORD.
verses.after: The people of Sodom were wicked and sinned greatly against the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now the people of Sodom were exceedingly wicked, sinners against the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve timing and all four directions.
verses.before: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, “Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,
verses.after: After Lot had separated from Abram, the LORD said to Abram, “Look from where you are: north, south, east, and west.
verses.tsw_comparator: The LORD said to Abram, after Lot had separated from him, “Lift up your eyes and look from the place where you are, northward and southward and eastward and westward,

verses.rationale: Keep land, both recipients, and the enduring promise.
verses.before: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.
verses.after: All the land you see I will give to you and your descendants forever.
verses.tsw_comparator: for all the land that you see I will give to you and to your offspring forever.

verses.rationale: Retain walking, both dimensions, and reason.

verses.rationale: Retain Mamre, Hebron, and altar; use the same tree rendering as 12:6.

verses.rationale: Unfold the names and alliance without identifying Hebrew beyond the title.

verses.before: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring possess the gate of people who hate them.”
verses.after: They blessed Rebekah, saying, “Our sister, may you become thousands upon ten thousands! May your descendants possess the gate of those who hate them.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And they blessed Rebekah and said to her, “Our sister, may you become thousands of ten thousands, and may your offspring possess the gate of those who hate them.”

verses.rationale: Preserve the female companions and the repeated departure statement.
verses.before: Then Rebekah and her young women arose and rode on the camels and followed the man. Thus the servant took Rebekah and went his way.
verses.after: Rebekah and her young women got up, mounted the camels, and followed the man. The servant took Rebekah with him and left.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Rebekah and her young women arose and rode on the camels and followed the man. Thus the servant took Rebekah and went his way.

verses.rationale: Render the difficult coming-from-coming phrase provisionally, preserving both place names.
verses.before: Now Isaac had come from Beer-lahai-roi and was dwelling in the Negeb.
verses.after: Isaac had come from Beer-lahai-roi and was living in the Negev.
verses.tsw_comparator: Now Isaac had come from Beer-lahai-roi and was dwelling in the Negeb.

verses.rationale: Choose meditate for the rare verb, with walking or praying alternatives noted.
verses.before: Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening, and he lifted up his eyes and saw, and look, camels were coming.
verses.after: Toward evening Isaac went out into the field to meditate. He looked up and saw camels approaching.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Isaac went out to meditate in the field toward evening, and he lifted up his eyes and saw, and behold, camels were coming.

verses.rationale: Preserve the reciprocal seeing and dismounting, with the dialogue continuing.
verses.before: Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she dismounted from the camel
verses.after: Rebekah looked up and saw Isaac. She got down from her camel
verses.tsw_comparator: And Rebekah lifted up her eyes, and when she saw Isaac, she dismounted from the camel

verses.rationale: Retain question, identification, and veiling without invented motives.
verses.before: and said to the servant, “Who is that man, walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” So she took her veil and covered herself.
verses.after: and asked the servant, “Who is that man walking across the field to meet us?” “He is my master,” the servant answered. She took her veil and covered herself.
verses.tsw_comparator: and said to the servant, “Who is that man, walking in the field to meet us?” The servant said, “It is my master.” So she took her veil and covered herself.

verses.rationale: Keep the final report concise, as the source does.
verses.before: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.
verses.after: The servant told Isaac everything he had done.
verses.tsw_comparator: And the servant told Isaac all the things that he had done.

verses.rationale: Clarify the compact tent phrase and retain marriage, love, and comfort without making the chapter a modern romance.
verses.before: Then Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother and took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.
verses.after: Isaac brought Rebekah into the tent of his mother Sarah. He took Rebekah as his wife and loved her. Isaac found comfort after his mother's death.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Isaac brought her into the tent of Sarah his mother and took Rebekah, and she became his wife, and he loved her. So Isaac was comforted after his mother’s death.

verses.rationale: Retain the additional marriage without asserting an unprovided date.
verses.before: Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.
verses.after: Abraham took another wife, named Keturah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abraham took another wife, whose name was Keturah.

verses.rationale: Retain this clear name list after source review; no change is needed for distinctiveness alone.
verses.before: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.after: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.
verses.tsw_comparator: She bore him Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

verses.rationale: Keep both generations and collective group names.
verses.before: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.after: Jokshan became the father of Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's descendants were the Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jokshan fathered Sheba and Dedan. The sons of Dedan were Asshurim, Letushim, and Leummim.

verses.rationale: Preserve the five-name line and maternal summary.
verses.before: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.
verses.after: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were Keturah's descendants.
verses.tsw_comparator: The sons of Midian were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All these were the sons of Keturah.

verses.rationale: Keep the comprehensive inheritance statement beside the following gifts.
verses.before: Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.
verses.after: Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abraham gave all that he had to Isaac.

verses.rationale: Preserve plural concubines, gifts, separation, timing, and repeated eastern direction.
verses.before: But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he still lived he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the land of the east.
verses.after: But Abraham gave gifts to the sons of his concubines. While he was still alive, he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the land of the east.
verses.tsw_comparator: But to the sons of his concubines Abraham gave gifts, and while he still lived he sent them away from his son Isaac, eastward to the land of the east.

verses.rationale: Retain the full stated lifespan.
verses.before: These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life: one hundred seventy-five years.
verses.after: Abraham lived 175 years in all.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the days of the years of Abraham’s life: one hundred seventy-five years.

verses.rationale: Preserve death and gathered-to-people as distinct expressions without reducing the latter to burial.
verses.before: Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and full, and was gathered to his people.
verses.after: He breathed his last and died at a good old age, old and full of years, and was gathered to his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: Abraham breathed his last and died in a good old age, an old man and full, and was gathered to his people.

verses.rationale: Keep both sons together and the complete property provenance.
verses.before: Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre,
verses.after: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite, facing Mamre.
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac and Ishmael his sons buried him in the cave of Machpelah, in the field of Ephron the son of Zohar the Hittite, east of Mamre,

verses.rationale: Retain the purchase reminder and shared burial.
verses.before: the field that Abraham purchased from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried, with Sarah his wife.
verses.after: This was the field Abraham had bought from the Hittites. Abraham and his wife Sarah were buried there.
verses.tsw_comparator: the field that Abraham purchased from the Hittites. There Abraham was buried, with Sarah his wife.

verses.rationale: Preserve passing blessing and the location linked earlier to Hagar.
verses.before: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son. And Isaac settled at Beer-lahai-roi.
verses.after: After Abraham died, God blessed his son Isaac. Isaac settled by Beer-lahai-roi.
verses.tsw_comparator: After the death of Abraham, God blessed Isaac his son. And Isaac settled at Beer-lahai-roi.

verses.rationale: Keep the family formula, both parents, nationality, and status.
verses.before: These are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.
verses.after: This is the account of Ishmael's family. He was Abraham's son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah's slave woman, bore to Abraham.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, whom Hagar the Egyptian, Sarah’s servant, bore to Abraham.

verses.rationale: Retain birth ordering and firstborn designation.
verses.before: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, named in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael; and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
verses.after: These are the names of Ishmael's sons in order of their birth: Nebaioth, Ishmael's firstborn, then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the names of the sons of Ishmael, named in the order of their birth: Nebaioth, the firstborn of Ishmael; and Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

verses.rationale: Retain this clear name list after source review; no change is needed for distinctiveness alone.
verses.before: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
verses.after: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,
verses.tsw_comparator: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

verses.rationale: Retain this clear name list after source review; no change is needed for distinctiveness alone.
verses.before: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
verses.after: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.
verses.tsw_comparator: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

verses.rationale: Retain both settlement terms and the twelve-leader connection to 17:20.
verses.before: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.
verses.after: These were Ishmael's sons, named by their settlements and encampments: twelve leaders of their peoples.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the sons of Ishmael and these are their names, by their villages and by their encampments, twelve princes according to their tribes.

verses.rationale: Preserve his lifespan and the same death idioms used for Abraham.
verses.before: These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
verses.after: Ishmael lived 137 years. He breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the years of the life of Ishmael: one hundred thirty-seven years. He breathed his last and died, and was gathered to his people.

verses.rationale: Choose settlement sense for the difficult final fell clause and collective referent; retain facing as in 16:12.
verses.before: They settled from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt in the direction of Assyria. He settled over against all his kinsmen.
verses.after: His descendants settled from Havilah to Shur, facing Egypt as you go toward Assyria. They lived facing all their brothers.
verses.tsw_comparator: They settled from Havilah to Shur, which is opposite Egypt in the direction of Assyria. He settled over against all his kinsmen.

verses.rationale: Preserve the family formula and repeated father-son relationship.
verses.before: These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham fathered Isaac,
verses.after: This is the account of Isaac's family. Isaac was Abraham's son; Abraham became the father of Isaac.
verses.tsw_comparator: These are the generations of Isaac, Abraham’s son: Abraham fathered Isaac,

verses.rationale: Retain age, all kinship, both Aramean titles, and region.
verses.before: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.
verses.after: Isaac was forty when he married Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean from Paddan-aram and the sister of Laban the Aramean.
verses.tsw_comparator: and Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah, the daughter of Bethuel the Aramean of Paddan-aram, the sister of Laban the Aramean, to be his wife.

verses.rationale: Keep prayer/answer repetition and conception without assigning fault.
verses.before: Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD granted his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.
verses.after: Isaac pleaded with the LORD for his wife because she could not bear children. The LORD answered his plea, and his wife Rebekah conceived.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Isaac prayed to the LORD for his wife, because she was barren. And the LORD granted his prayer, and Rebekah his wife conceived.

verses.rationale: Retain the force and incompleteness of her question without supplying a diagnosis or unstated destination.
verses.before: The children struggled together within her, and she said, “If it is thus, why is this happening to me?” So she went to inquire of the LORD.
verses.after: The children struggled against each other inside her. “If it is like this, why am I here?” she said. So she went to inquire of the LORD.
verses.tsw_comparator: The children struggled together within her, and she said, “If it is thus, why is this happening to me?” So she went to inquire of the LORD.

verses.rationale: Preserve paired nations and the conventional subject reading of the older/younger clause, flagged for review.
verses.before: And the LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you will be divided; the one will be stronger than the other, the older will serve the younger.”
verses.after: The LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb; two peoples will separate from within you. One people will be stronger than the other, and the older will serve the younger.”
verses.tsw_comparator: And the LORD said to her, “Two nations are in your womb, and two peoples from within you shall be divided; the one shall be stronger than the other, the older shall serve the younger.”

verses.rationale: Keep fulfilled time and the revealed twin pregnancy.
verses.before: When her days to give birth were completed, look, there were twins in her womb.
verses.after: When her time to give birth arrived, there were twins in her womb.
verses.tsw_comparator: When her days to give birth were completed, behold, there were twins in her womb.

verses.rationale: Retain red and hair imagery without inventing an etymology for Esau.
verses.before: The first came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they called his name Esau.
verses.after: The first came out red, covered all over like a hairy cloak. They named him Esau.
verses.tsw_comparator: The first came out red, all his body like a hairy cloak, so they called his name Esau.

verses.rationale: Keep heel/name connection, unnamed naming agent, and paternal age.
verses.before: Afterward his brother came out, with his hand holding Esau’s heel, so his name was called Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.
verses.after: Then his brother came out, his hand gripping Esau's heel. He was named Jacob. Isaac was sixty when they were born.
verses.tsw_comparator: Afterward his brother came out, with his hand holding Esau’s heel, so his name was called Jacob. Isaac was sixty years old when she bore them.

verses.rationale: Choose quiet for tam without making the contrast a verdict of moral innocence.
verses.before: When the boys grew up, Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.
verses.after: The boys grew up. Esau became a skilled hunter, a man of the open country, while Jacob was a quiet man who lived in tents.
verses.tsw_comparator: When the boys grew up, Esau was a skillful hunter, a man of the field, while Jacob was a quiet man, dwelling in tents.

verses.rationale: Render game-in-mouth idiom naturally and preserve unequal stated reasons.
verses.before: Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.after: Isaac loved Esau because he enjoyed the game Esau brought, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Isaac loved Esau because he ate of his game, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

verses.rationale: Keep the cooking scene and Esau's physical condition.
verses.before: Once when Jacob was cooking stew, Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.
verses.after: Jacob was cooking a stew when Esau came in from the open country, exhausted.
verses.tsw_comparator: Once when Jacob was cooking stew, Esau came in from the field, and he was exhausted.

verses.rationale: Retain emphatic red repetition and name explanation.
verses.before: Esau said to Jacob, “Let me gulp down some of that red stew, for I am exhausted!” Therefore his name was called Edom.
verses.after: Esau said to Jacob, “Please let me gulp down some of that red stuff—that red stuff! I am exhausted.” That is why he was called Edom.
verses.tsw_comparator: And Esau said to Jacob, “Let me gulp down some of that red stew, for I am exhausted!” Therefore his name was called Edom.

verses.rationale: Keep the demand and its priority in the exchange.
verses.before: Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright now.”
verses.after: Jacob answered, “First sell me your birthright.”
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob said, “Sell me your birthright now.”

verses.rationale: Preserve his claimed danger and dismissive question as character speech.
verses.before: Esau said, “I am about to die; of what use is a birthright to me?”
verses.after: “I am about to die,” Esau said. “What use is a birthright to me?”
verses.tsw_comparator: Esau said, “I am about to die; of what use is a birthright to me?”

verses.rationale: Keep the oath before the sale.
verses.before: Jacob said, “Swear to me now.” So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.
verses.after: “Swear to me first,” Jacob said. Esau swore and sold his birthright to Jacob.
verses.tsw_comparator: Jacob said, “Swear to me now.” So he swore to him and sold his birthright to Jacob.

verses.rationale: Retain every rapid action and the narrator's explicit final judgment.
verses.before: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank and rose and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
verses.after: Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew. Esau ate and drank, got up, and went away. So Esau treated his birthright with contempt.
verses.tsw_comparator: Then Jacob gave Esau bread and lentil stew, and he ate and drank and rose and went his way. Thus Esau despised his birthright.
